summary: Chamath acknowledges OpenAI is technically ahead of everyone and commands crazy valuations, but argues its recurring drama and massive employee secondary sales before a fully functional business exists reveal a rational but ethically fraught organizational culture that creates structural tension.
quote: They're technically ahead of everybody else. A lot of people want to put in money at crazy prices. A bunch of that value is transferred immediately to the employees who circle the wagons and do what's necessary to keep the taps flowing.

summary: Chamath observes that McDonald's stock is way up because it has aggressively raised prices — rewarding shareholders while squeezing customers — reflecting that the company has been motivated and rewarded for prioritizing shareholder returns.
quote: These guys have jacked up prices. If you look at what's happened to the stock, the stock is way up. They've been very motivated and rewarded as a company for just rewarding the shareholder and screwing over the customer.
